contract_verdict: AGREE with the contract's direction: a distinct exact experiment field, no feature/output/dimension/haptic requests, a sealed writer with no HID scheduler, the T1 supervisor left unchanged, a new finite supervisor that requires the actual child and its SPI parent, exit 77 before the compositor on missing readiness, the same closed cleanup and recovery, and no input or panel claim.

contract_comments.text: The mouse node is shared, so endpoint existence cannot attribute origin. Any started event service with a Generic Desktop Mouse usage pair requests /dev/usb_hid_mouse (rev002 IOHIDEventService.cpp pdHIDPublishSupportedQueues -> PDHIDPublishMouseDevice). The supervisor's readiness must therefore come from the registry: IOHIDDevice services exactly [PDM1SPIHID, <child class>], the child's registry provider is that PDM1SPIHID instance, PDSerialHID 0 and no other HID device class. It also needs the rev002 queue line 'ready kind=2' after BSD ready. Node presence alone must not count.

Settle the boot-argument dependency as one closed combination. The child requires the adapter probe (pdm1kbd=1) and the interface-2 descriptor (enumeration). Recommended: a distinct child token, accepted only together with pdm1kbd=1 and pdm1trackpadenum=1. The adapter refuses the child without enumeration, and the host appends it only under the exact new field (exclusive with DART and with the T1-only field). No child token for any existing packet.
Opening both nodes moves keyboard and mouse input away from the text console, as the keyboard node already does. Inventory before the compositor must stay stat-only for both nodes.

source_facts_for_lifecycle_design.text: IOHIDDevice::start sets _workLoop = getWorkLoop(), retains it and adds its IOHIDEventSource (IOHIDDevice.cpp:354-361). A child attached to the PDM1SPIHID instance that does not override getWorkLoop inherits PDM1SPIHID::getWorkLoop() = transportLoop, the same loop the parent's poll timer runs on. Delivering child reports from poll() then gives same-loop ownership without new locks. A child attached elsewhere (for example IOResources) would get a different loop; avoid that.

Parent order: IOHIDDevice::start -> handleStart (enumeration inside transportGate->runAction) -> descriptor parse -> interfaces -> publishProperties -> first-match notifier -> registerService (L364-478). Then PDM1SPIHID::start sets published=true and arms the 2 ms poll timer (adapter L117-121). Creating or starting a child inside handleStart/startGated would run its start (addEventSource, registerService, matching) while the parent holds its own gate and before the parent is registered, risking deadlock and ordering problems. Recommended: create, attach and start the child only after super::start(provider) returns true, outside the gate and before the poll timer is armed. Enable routing with a gated child-ready flag set only after child start succeeds.

On any start failure IOHIDDevice::start calls stop(provider) on itself (L482-486). The parent must then keep routing disabled, detach and release its reference, and leave device-2 traffic in the existing otherMessages path (adapter L323-327: consumed, never relabeled). The design must decide explicitly whether a child failure fails the parent. Either choice must leave the keyboard path byte-unchanged, and the supervisor must then exit 77 before the compositor.

Parent fail() sets stopping and stops the hardware but keeps services registered, so a child would stay registered with no further reports. On termination IOKit stops clients before providers, so the child's IOHIDDevice::stop (removing its event source from transportLoop, L541-544) runs before PDM1SPIHID::handleStop/quiesce/disposeTransport. Required: clear the parent's child pointer in a gated action (the stopGated pattern) during child willTerminate/stop, so poll() never dereferences a stopping child. disposeTransport must not release transportLoop while the child still holds it (the child releases it in free). No panic path should be reachable from child teardown.

Route a device-2 input message only when its report ID is one the descriptor declares and its length equals that report's declared size including the ID: 0x02 = 8, 0x3f = 17, 0x44 = 1752 (Astra's descriptor review). The advertised max_input 2048 is a diagnostic since core 002 and must not size or accept anything. The existing device-1 filter m1kbd_keyboard_input must stay device-1 only. The 8-message, 2 ms poll budget also bounds 1752-byte reports.

The child must answer setReport/getReport (and any property-driven output) with kIOReturnUnsupported locally, never forwarding to the parent's waitResponse/dlsp encoder. Its newReportDescriptor must return exactly descriptor_bytes from the parent's owned snapshot, and only when result == ENUM_OK and stage == COMPLETE. Report 0x02's Mouse collection will start an event driver and publish the mouse node (C1); 0x3f Digitizer Touch Pad and vendor 0x44 publish nothing.
